tldr: Most teams use Google Analytics because it's free, not because they chose it. Mixpanel is about as easy to set up, has a generous free tier and a startup plan, and answers the product questions GA can't — what a user did inside your product, and whether they came back.
faq: Why do most teams still use Google Analytics?
Because it's free. It's worth asking honestly: if GA weren't free, how many teams would pick it over the alternatives?
Is Mixpanel harder to set up than GA?
No — it's about as easy. That's one of the most common reasons founders give for staying on GA, and it doesn't hold up.
Contrary to the assumption, there's a generous free tier and a startup plan. Cost is rarely the real blocker.
What can Mixpanel answer that GA can't?

What a user actually did inside your product, in what order, and whether they came back. GA is built for traffic and marketing — where visitors came from and which campaign drove them — and it's good at that, not at product behaviour.
You can, and many teams do — GA for acquisition, a product analytics tool for behaviour. What you shouldn't do is run two product analytics tools and end up with two sources of truth.
